question: Should OpenClaw add a new internal `session:end` hook event, or should workflow integrations use the existing typed plugin `session_end` lifecycle hook instead?
rationale: Both surfaces can support session-completion automation, but adding an internal hook changes the operator automation API while the existing plugin hook appears to be the current runtime lifecycle contract.

options.title: Use plugin session_end as the contract
options.body: Document typed plugin `session_end` as the supported completion hook for workflow integrations and close or retitle this issue after that decision is visible.

options.title: Approve an internal session:end event
options.body: Define a narrow internal hook event shape and wire it consistently across reset, delete, shutdown, cron/webhook, agent.send, and subagent completion paths with focused tests.

options.title: Wait for linked PR review
options.body: Keep this issue open until the linked daily/idle reset PR is landed or closed, then reassess the remaining internal-hook gap.

recommendation.title: Use plugin session_end as the contract
recommendation.body: Document typed plugin `session_end` as the supported completion hook for workflow integrations and close or retitle this issue after that decision is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a hook/plugin API-boundary decision, and Vincent Koc has the strongest current history and discussion signal for that boundary.
